div.p: Many people, even today, do not really know what they want. Propaganda, working through self-interest and force without regard for truth or fiction, takes possession of the mind which does not think for itself and so offers but weak resistance. It is inevitable that truth today must take on the form of propaganda in order to reach men’s ears. It is thus the great task of creative thinking to lay stress on the simple, fundamental truths, in order that they may echo in the intellect, with which all men are endowed.

In opposing the claim to absolute knowledge, philosophy has the task of keeping alive individual thought, and through it the personality of the individual which would be extinguished under totalitarian regimes. It must, indeed, remind every individual that he may find and develop his own personality, and that he ceases to be human, if he renounces this possibility. For the sake of our common future it is imperative that we should transform thought into action with enlightened motives and with the deepest sense of responsibility.
